answer: Verification starts when an agent requests work: three random peers each issue a micro-benchmark with a hard wall-clock deadline, say 400ms to train a tiny tensor to a fixed loss. Because the deadline binds to real elapsed time, a clone cannot multiplex one GPU across ten identities without each run finishing late, so the verifier discards any result past the cutoff. Each passing agent then seals its trace with a timber-signed receipt hashed into a shared mirror ledger every peer can re-check, and the stake that backed the run stays locked in a vault until the round clears.
